## Method and limits
- Window: 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31 (end exclusive 2026-06-01) [c1]. Today is 2026-10-23, so the data stops 145 days ago. Nothing here describes June to October 2026.
- Lane: news only. No research or case-count lane was used.
- Coverage: the table passed strict index partition reads at 107.1% of the historical row floor, but the tool says this is not a proof of ingest completeness [c1]. The tool treats May 2026 as complete (no partial period flag) [c1].
- Censoring: the cutoff was set at 2026-06-01 to avoid a false collapse in the newest month [c1]. Entity and geography labels are reliable only to 2026-05-01. In March and April 2026 country fill was 36.3% and 40.1% [c1].
- Match mode: "mention" for trends, themes, entities and geography. The sources panel and recent and critical items use "central" [c1]. The panels therefore cover different article sets.
- Placed share: 63.5% [c1]. Place rows may contain name collisions.
- What the counts are: articles in this corpus that mention measles, including duplicates (the Dhaka Tribune item appears twice in the recent feed) [c1].
- What they are not: they are not case counts, deaths, outbreak size, or vaccination rates. The deaths and cases quoted (for example 585 deaths in Bangladesh [c1]) are figures reported by the articles, not verified here.
- Interpretation (mine): the 2025 surge likely reflects the US outbreak and the political attention on Kennedy and the CDC, and the 2026 surge reflects Bangladesh and others. The data show co-occurrence only, not cause. The sampled headlines show Bangladesh, Pakistan, Chad and Maryland, but the sample is small.
- Not measurable here: coverage after 2026-05-31, whole-window publisher concentration, and the share of articles that are significant reporting rather than passing mentions.
